standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting a finite projective module over the quotient to a finite projective module over an etale extension which is an isomorphism on the quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the etale extension from which the module over the ring is built.

standard_prerequisites.name: Gabber's criterion for a henselian pair: every etale ring map inducing an isomorphism on the quotient has a section
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the section along which the lifted module is base changed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-NAK}, cited at proof lines 3376-3377
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes a lift of an isomorphism modulo the ideal surjective.

standard_prerequisites.name: A surjective endomorphism of a finite module that becomes invertible after tensoring with a nilpotent quotient is invertible
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-fun}, cited at proof lines 3378-3379
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the composition of the two surjections an isomorphism, hence both of them.

core_obligations: Prove the final statement: lift the given projective module to an etale extension and take a section to descend it (proof lines 3360-3372).
Deduce surjectivity of the reduction map on isomorphism classes (proof lines 3372-3373).
For injectivity, lift an isomorphism modulo the ideal to a map of the modules and show it is surjective by Nakayama (proof lines 3374-3377).
Construct the reverse surjection and conclude both are isomorphisms by the cancellation lemma (proof lines 3378-3380).
proof_roadmap: Surjectivity via etale lifting plus a section (proof lines 3360-3373).
Injectivity via Nakayama and cancellation (proof lines 3374-3380).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that reduction modulo the ideal of a henselian pair induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of finite projective modules over the ring and over its quotient. Surjectivity is the substance: the given finite projective module over the quotient is first lifted to a finite projective module over an etale extension which induces an isomorphism on the quotient, and since the pair is henselian that etale map has a section, along which the lifted module is base changed to produce the required module over the ring. Injectivity reduces to Nakayama and a standard cancellation: an isomorphism modulo the ideal lifts to a surjection by projectivity, a reverse surjection is constructed the same way, and the composition of the two is an isomorphism because it reduces to one, hence both maps are isomorphisms.
